extracted.intended_audience: machine learning researchers and data scientists working on startup outcome prediction, innovation finance analysts, and patent analytics researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and evaluating interpretable machine-learning models to predict startup outcomes (next funding, patent growth, exits) using firm-quarter panel data matched to patent records, with attention to avoiding temporal leakage, handling class imbalance, and producing transparent, reproducible rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prediction horizon definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Three horizons are evaluated: next funding within 12 months, patent-stock growth within 24 months, and exit through an initial public offering (IPO) or acquisition within 36 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly define time windows for each target outcome (e.g., 12m for funding, 24m for patent growth, 36m for exits) so model tasks and labels are clear and comparable across cohorts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset construction and linking
rubrics_metrics.description: A firm-quarter panel for 2010-2023 is constructed from Crunchbase and matched to U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build a panel dataset with consistent temporal granularity (firm-quarter), and link firm-level data sources (e.g., Crunchbase) to patent records (USPTO) to create features and targets grounded in external authoritative data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprocessing and temporal leakage avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprocessing is fit on a development window (2010-2019) and applied without change to later cohorts to avoid leakage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fit all preprocessing (feature selection, normalization, imputations, encoders, etc.) only on the development period and then apply the exact transformations to holdout/cohort periods; do not refit on later data to prevent information leakage across time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class imbalance handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Class imbalance is addressed using inverse-prevalence weights and the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique for Nominal and Continuous features (SMOTE-NC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When outcomes are imbalanced, use sample weighting (inverse-prevalence) and/or oversampling methods appropriate for mixed data (SMOTE-NC) to reduce bias toward majority class; document procedures and parameters used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model selection and baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: Logistic regression and tree ensembles, including Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost, are compared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both linear baselines (e.g., logistic regression) and a set of state-of-the-art tree ensemble methods for comparative evaluation; report hyperparameter tuning protocols and selection criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics: PR-AUC and AUROC
rubrics_metrics.description: Models are compared using the area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC) and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both PR-AUC and AUROC — PR-AUC is particularly informative for imbalanced prediction tasks; provide per-target metric values and, where useful, confidence intervals or variance across folds/cohorts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting predictive performance by outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent, funding, and exit predictions achieve AUROC values of 0.921, 0.817, and 0.872, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present performance separately for each target/outcome so readers can compare difficulty and model effectiveness across tasks; include both summary metrics and more detailed diagnostics (precision/recall at operating points, calibration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretability and transparent rankings
rubrics_metrics.description: An interpretable machine learning framework is developed to provide transparent and reproducible rankings for innovation finance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt interpretable methods or explainability tools (feature importances, shapley values, rule extraction, etc.) to produce rankings that stakeholders can inspect; emphasize transparency in how rankings are derived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and provision of code/data
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper emphasizes transparent and reproducible rankings and includes links/toggles for code, data, and media associated with the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide code, data access instructions, and model artifacts or seeds so that results can be reproduced; document preprocessing, cohort splits, and evaluation scripts.
